quotes.excerpt: Killer Influences #1 stands out by blending societies true crime obsession with influencer culture in a way that feels both unsettling and original. Joey Esposito crafts a chilling tale, while Valeria Burzo and Iñaki Azpiazu really bring the story together with excellent illustrations and color. Killer Influences is a gripping true crime story turning fame and fear into a dangerously addictive pact.

All in all, fans of dark comedy and true crime will find Killer Influences bloody hilarious. More sensitive souls need not apply. However, if you’re a fan of Only Murders in the Building, this will be up your alley.

I finished Beast of Borikén #2 knowing more about Borikén culture, and being entirely interested in it, than I did going in without ever feeling lectured to. That is the real accomplishment. Anta has built a horror comic that works as cultural preservation, handing readers the names and practices his story's villains are trying to bulldoze. The monster backdrop works because the culture keeping it alive is true. I want to see where Loli’s adventure goes next, and I trust this team to keep making me want more.
If you’ve read this comic, let me know down in the comments. Make sure to like, subscribe, and follow Fanlight Zone on all platforms.And until next time...Read Your Comics.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This is a ripping yard of piracy and sorcery, which highlights an often overlooked aspect of Conan’s background and the true character of Valeria of the Red Brotherhood. The artwork holds to the same standard of detail and drive. If you think of Conan as little more than a big, dumb barbarian, prepare to be educated!

After a long, strange journey, 'Is Ted OK?' concludes with a massively satisfying final issue, showcasing the book's identity, intent, and innovation that has made this book one of 2026's biggest standouts.

Is Ted OK? #6 sticks the landing and brings an amazing ending to this unique and awesome series. The uniqueness of the story brings readers in, but the drama and emotions are what really keep readers hooked. The ending is fitting and conclusive but does leave the door open to return to this world as well. I for one would welcome another chapter of this amazing story. If you are like me and have been reading this series issue by issue, you will be very happy with this conclusion to the story. However, if you sat this one out, I’ve got great options for you, get to your local shop and hope they have all 6 issues, wait for the Trade Paperback and enjoy, or head over to Neon Ichiban and get every issue NOW! No matter what you ultimately choose, one thing is for sure you need to read this series in its entirety.

Lost Fantasy continues to rank in my top five comics of this year. The storytelling within this series continues to grow in ways that you generally wouldn’t consider it going. Which adds to the entertainment and curiosity of what is to come. The way the Hunter Families are separate but somewhat similar in their family struggles is very interesting to see. Building on the notion that we may have different life styles, but have the same struggles behind closed doors. Astonishing issue, make sure you snag this at your local comic book shop!

Henry brings the violence as a deadly showdown forces his hand as Edge continues his reign of terror. The writing delves into the conflict on a very high level. The art showcases the major conflicts evolving. Brace for impact with that final page!

Bleeding Hearts #6 is equal parts terrifying and emotional. Poke is forced to make decisions and more is revealed as to what is happening with him. This issue ramps up the intensity and is fast paced taking us into unknown territories.

Poke’s world crashes down around him as Outbreak Day brings sorrow instead of joy. Camp pens a heavily emotional tale with phenomenal writing. Morian & Hollingsworth never shy away from the grittiness and difficult choices of this world. An amazing display of powerful storytelling.

Ultimately, A Mischief of Magpies is a haunting and beautiful book that goes far beyond merely being simply a solid fantasy. It’s an immersive story that resonates on so many levels. There’s a magic to this book that will break your heart—and it might be one of the best books to come out this year.
A Mischief Of Magpies #1 is perfection and sticks out as one of the best comics of the year so far. A must get.

Acknowledging how this altered kryptonite is now affecting and infecting the entire planet really elevates the scale of Zod’s threat in Superman Unlimited #16. The multiple story elements coming together also feels very organic which just adds the enjoyment of it all.

Zod isn’t satisfied with his current victories and the Super family is scrambling to stop him! Slott exposes more of Zod’s schemes with a great script. Scott & the team keep events rolling with a steady balance of drama and action. There’s no turning back now!
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

The story is great, the art is stunning, and it’s a trial by fire for Superboy Prime that makes me more confident than ever that this character is actually here to stay. Just an amazing turnaround for this once-hated figure.

Superman #39 is a can’t-miss issue for this Spring’s biggest event. This issue sets up exciting new things for the DC Universe. This is an all-star creative team, and it feels like they are not holding back their talents at all with this arc.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!
Power Rangers Unlimited #1 is a bold, legacy embracing start which easily grabs hold of the best of BOOM!-era Power Rangers comics and presents it from a fresh and exciting angle.

Power Rangers Unlimited #1 delivers an action-packed debut that leans into Power Rangers history from a fresh point of view, and when combined with the out-of-this-world art and extensive roster, Power Rangers Unlimited becomes a must-read for any and every fan of the franchise.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

We get our first hints of how this fits in with the rest of the Absolute Universe just as it ends, but this feels much more like an evergreen, one-of-a-kind comic that people will be talking about for years.

Camp, Rodríguez and Otsmane-Elhaou leave readers with an intense read unlike anything else seen in the comics landscape currently. A phenomenal script gels perfectly with Rodríguez’s incredible art yet again. While its’ a bittersweet moment with the series on hold/over, readers leave with an overwhelming sense of the true direction of superhero comics for years to come. Highest possible recommendation.
Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 is a compelling mix of magic and spy fiction, packed with haunting imagery and a unique mystery.

Black Tower: The Raven Conspiracy #1 proves that everything out of DC Vertigo should be jumped on immediately. This was a strong start to a comic series that has captured my attention from the first page and didn’t let go until the ending. I cannot recommend this comic enough!

Absolute Superman #23 is hard hitting and intense as Kal-El is hunting Braniac, who is always ahead of him by mere seconds. The mind games mix into reality and pushes Superman in a way I don’t believe any of us have ever seen in a comic before. This issue will leave you sitting and thinking with your own thoughts and is one that should be talked about as one of the most powerful superhero issue of the year.

An unthinkable evil forces Superman to question his ethics while searching for Brainiac! Aaron challenges the soul of hope with a superb script. Ferreyra unlocks a wide array of responses to the troubles brought forth. A stunning look at the Intricacy of hope in the Absolute Universe.

To save Gotham City, Batman jumps into a fire raging out of control. Fraction lights the match with an incredible script. Scalera and Morey bring breathtaking action on each page. The Dark Knight has never seen a fight like this before.

Batman #13 is a bit of a fast paced issue, but nonetheless a joy to read. Sometimes the issues that go too fast feel lackluster. And other times, they're like this – where little happens narratively but the things that do happen are frankly so dang cool that it's absolutely worth it. As a result, my only true gripe is that if you're not interested in this event, I'd say this one's worth skipping. But if you are? Buckle up and enjoy the ride.

Rook Exodus remains one of those titles where the end result is always worth the wait even if it takes way longer than readers would like. Another break is slated following the end of this arc, which hopefully will arrive before the end of 2026. Even then, it will likely result in one of the strongest issues that month.

Rook: Exodus #11 is a tense and exciting issue that balances strong character conflict with big, chaotic action. Geoff Johns keeps the emotional stakes high as the team struggles with trust, guilt, and survival, while Jason Fabok makes the spider attack feel dangerous and overwhelming. With a strong cliffhanger and plenty of momentum, this issue sets up the next issue in a major way. If you are like me and have fallen off from reading this series for one reason or another, it’s time to get back into it. The excitement and drama are at a fever pitch and promise to only build up more. This should be on top of your list when headed to the shop this week.

The secret life of Emily Hawke is revealed as more questions loom in the horizon. Ewing dips away from Jo’s story to weave in a throwback tale. Lindsey returns with a solid showcase of the insanity of 1943. Where things go from here are anyone’s gamble.

Absolute Green Lantern remains somewhat difficult to grasp, but this issue is relatively digestible. It features a throwback mad scientist story while continuing to build what seems to be a far-reaching conspiracy.

Captain America #15 is a satisfying penultimate issue in the Hell’s Angel arc. Challenging Steve Rogers’ moral compass in the shadow of Doom is as bold a creative choice as the creative team could make, and it lands solidly. I wish issue 16 was dropping tomorrow so I could see how this arc ends.

Captain America #15 is a thrill ride from beginning to end, and features a few twists that fans won't see coming. How it all shakes out remains to be seen, but it's looking like Chip Zdarsky intends to put Steve Rogers through Hell in more ways than one.

Escape #9 is another gripping chapter in a series that understands how war can distort fear, trust, and humanity. Rick Remender introduces Flynn as an unpredictable new element whose experiences behind enemy lines lead to some deeply tragic moments, while Daniel Acuña makes every encounter feel dangerously immediate. The contrast between Flynn and Milton is especially compelling now that Milton has learned to see humanity in those he once considered monsters. Flynn's sudden shift toward ruthlessness could use more development, but the tension it creates leaves the series in an incredibly precarious place.
Ryan North continues to craft a legendary Fantastic Four run. Each issue is so different yet they all work. The stories are unique, refreshing, and enjoyable
All in all, a fun journey through space and its consequences for the Fantastic Four. A good classic-style story before the DNX crossover begins!

As “Bad Seeds” takes hold, Cassandra Cain makes a dangerous attempt to help. Brombal delivers an exceptional look at the hero behind the mask. Miyazawa & Castro craft the terrors with strong art sequences. An exciting adventure begins here!

Daredevil #6 is a warm-up with Murdock getting no time for relaxation in the city that never sleeps. Fans are going to love the final page of this book, and overall this run has found its footing in terms of tone and the right amount of fun blended with action.

Daredevil #6 launches a new arc and brings back some old foes, but it never loses the forward momentum that makes this title a standout. If you haven't added it to your pull list, now's the perfect time.

Rogue Sun #35 delivers what might be its best issue yet, as it features a major status quo change that ties into the series' key themes. While Rogue Sun is going on a hiatus until 2027, it's primed to deliver some truly great stories when it returns.

Ahmed and Ohta reunite to take Logan on a multiversal adventure. While the comic feels more in-line with something from Spider-Verse rather than classic Wolverine, that’s exactly what makes it refreshing.
King Spawn #58 centers its story on a not-so-dynamic duo, as the horror and mystery ramp up

reason.snippet: The Deadman #4 takes Boston Brand from Hell to Heaven and delivers another entertaining mix of supernatural mystery, dark comedy, and character development. W. Maxwell Prince continues to give Deadman a fresh voice, while Martin Morazzo and Chris O’Halloran make the afterlife visually unforgettable. The story moves the Mr. Juan mystery forward and finishes with a fantastic cliffhanger involving Sw…
pros: Hilarious Deadman and Bobby interactions
Creative interpretation of Heaven as Morazzo and O’Halloran continue to deliver incredible visuals
Strong development of the Mr. Juan/Ghost Things mystery
Fun cliffhanger that makes the next issue a must-read
cons: The larger mystery continues to move slowly, although the extra issues should help

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The book combines biting parodies of Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, as well as fandom itself, with some great superhero action as a new Lovecraftian-style menace rises.
pros: Steve Skroce's art is a great as usual, a wonderful mix of the realistic and the surreal.
Stan Lee's flamboyant personality is lovingly (and hilariously) parodied in the character of Stu Reeds.
I liked the design of the heroes in the book and look forward to seeing more of them.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: All in all, a fun journey through space and its consequences for the Fantastic Four. A good classic-style story before the DNX crossover begins!
pros: Compelling story, makes the First Family have to choose between the truth and what's best for an entire planet
A love letter to visitor from another world stories, particularly Star Trek
cons: A cheeky gripe: I wish this story was longer!

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Christopher Priest, Joe Quesada, and Richard Isanove deliver a beautiful, tragic finale as Ketema and T'Challa face off one last time with the fate of Wakanda and the world in the balance.
pros: Joe Quesada's art is breathtaking, delivering on a number of emotional beats.
Christopher Priest deftly uses faith to examine humanity through the characters of T'Challa and Ketema.
Richard Isanove's color art delivers on a technical level and an emotional one.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Captain America #15 is a thrill ride from beginning to end, and features a few twists that fans won't see coming. How it all shakes out remains to be seen, but it's looking like Chip Zdarsky intends to put Steve Rogers through Hell in more ways than one.
pros: Zdarsky has a good grip on Steve Rogers' character, while also pushing him in new directions.
Schiti returns, delivering intense battles from beginning to end and hellish imagery, backed up by Fajardo Jr. scolor work.
A massive twist that nobody will see coming.
cons: The ending feels a little too on the nose.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Venom #261 takes a surprisingly personal detour during Queen in Black to finally confront the bad blood between Venom and Reed Richards. Al Ewing finds plenty to unpack in their shared history, allowing Venom's anger to boil over before giving both characters an opportunity to reckon with mistakes made long ago. The extended opening recap eats up valuable space, and it's a little strange watching…
pros: Finally addresses the unresolved history between Venom and Reed Richards
Ewing gives Venom's anger convincing emotional weight
Reed's willingness to acknowledge his mistakes adds depth to the confrontation
cons: The five-page opening recap takes up too much of the issue
The training-room sequence feels oddly relaxed given the crisis unfolding outside

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Marvel Zombies: War Zone #1 lives up to its name as it delivers plenty of grit and gore, as the Punisher fights through a zombie-infested New York. Whether this is your first or latest exposure to the world of Marvel Zombies, you'll walk away satisfied.
pros: Waltz mixes the grit of a Punisher story with the overwhelming gore of a Marvel Zombies story.
Jamie Infante proves to be more than up to the task of drawing superhero zombies – and the carnage that follows in their wake.
Valenza's color art is perfectly muted, save for the bright red buckets of blood spilled throughout.
A unique twist that sets this apart from other Marvel Zombies stories.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Marvel Mangaverse: Web of Blood #1 brings the Mangaverse back with an ambitious, magic-fueled apocalypse that packs a surprising amount into its opening chapter. The worldbuilding can get dense, but there's enough action to keep things moving, particularly whenever Laura Kinney cuts loose. Kenny Ruiz delivers huge manga-inspired battles that eventually reach kaiju proportions, while Noiry and Aria…
pros: Easy jumping-on point despite the extensive lore
A creative magical reinvention of the Marvel Universe
Laura Kinney is immediately compelling and incredibly badass
Kenny Ruiz's manga-influenced artwork fits the concept extremely well
cons: The ultimate consequence of all the fighting isn't especially surprising
Heavy worldbuilding can make portions of the issue feel dense

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: By embracing the chaotic status quos of both heroes, Black Panther/Namor: Doomed #1 delivers a stylish and entertaining first chapter.
pros: Ethan S. Parker and Griffin Sheridan explore a T'Challa who is a bit more playful than recent characterizations.
Stefano Nesi's artwork flows and delivers in both the character beats and action scenes.
Jesus Aburtov's color choices are stellar, bringing extra vibrancy to the story
cons: The straightforwardness of the dialogue might feel a bit out of place to readers used to a more refined Wakandan lexicon.

reason.snippet: Spawn #378 slows things down to establish the players circling Al Simmons while reinforcing just how dangerous the world has become. Much of the issue will feel familiar to longtime readers, particularly the recap of Al's past, but the vampire meeting and mysterious butcher keep the larger story intriguing. Stephen Segovia makes the most of the limited action, delivering a ferocious finish that re…
pros: Stephen Segovia delivers excellent Spawn action
The vampire gangster adds an interesting wrinkle to the new status quo
Helpful recap for newer or returning readers
cons: Al's backstory recap may feel redundant for regular readers

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: ‘Zatanna’ #5 brings Zatanna back to The Hidden City of the Homo Magi where she has to confront her feelings over losing her mother while trying to save the city.
pros: Zatanna's personality and emotions were able to shine a bit more during this issue
Jamal Campbell and Andrew Dalhouse were able to create a truly terrifying scene of the flame spirit
Zatanna's grief manifesting in anger was beautifully written and isn't something we see often.
cons: I wish the flame spirit and its connection to the Hidden City was explored more in this issue rather than leaving it for the next issue.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: A triumphant return of the Cosmic Marvel icon, crafted with genuine love of the source material while also blazing a new trail of ideas for ROM's adventures.
pros: ROM ends up feeling exactly as he should
The artwork is fantastic and fluid with great design work on ROM's new look especially
There is a clear feeling of reverence and love for the source material while still trying to do something new
cons: It took a minute for ROM's characterization to settle in
